item.title: An Ackland Odyssey — Thu Nov 19, 3:00 PM — Ackland Art Museum
item.description:
This program is now FULL. To be added to our WAITLIST, please email acklandRSVP@unc.edu.
How have artists represented the characters from Homer’s Odyssey through the centuries? How do images translate and adapt the words from this epic poem for new, diverse audiences? Professors Timothy Shea and Hérica Valladares, both from UNC-Chapel Hill’s Department of Classics with adjunct appointments in the Department of Art and Art History, will lead a seminar-style discussion focusing on works from the museum’s collection, ranging from an ancient Greek vase fragment to a twentieth-century lithograph by American artist Benton Spruance. Free, registration required below.
This event is part of UNC–Chapel Hill’s Campus Life Experience (CLE) program. Students who attend can scan the QR code provided at the event to receive CLE credit.
Source: UNC Chapel Hill

The Research Administrators Peer-to-Peer (RAPP) group seeks to create a community of practice for research administrators and other professionals involved in research administration across the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. The group will participate in meetings and other activities to inform, educate, and support individuals by providing a forum for discussion and an open exchange of ideas; an information network for policies, procedures, and sponsor guidelines; and networking opportunities for research administration professionals across campus.

item.description: Date: Saturday, December 5, 2026. Please also mark your calendar for a rain date on Sunday, December 6! Times: 9am to 5pm Join us in the search for one of North Carolina’s rarest salamanders, the federally threatened Neuse River waterdog, found only in the Neuse and Tar-Pamlico River Basins in North Carolina. Learn from expert biologists, explore the natural history of the waterdog, observe historically collected specimens and participate in field monitoring of the species. Discover how you can bring the excitement of field research of this rare species into your classroom. With support from the US Fish and Wildlife Service, Project RESTORE (Rescuing Endangered Species Through Outreach, Restoration, and Education) will feature a suite of educational opportunities for teachers and students to participate in restoration and monitoring of imperiled and endangered species in eastern North Carolina. item.title: Histotree — Tue Dec 8, 10:00 AM — Hammocks Beach State Park
item.description:

How does one determine the age of a tree without coring to count the rings? Join us to uncover the story of selected trees by estimating their age using yarn and some basic math skills (use that calculator app on your phone to help with the division & multiplication skills). item.title: Bill of Rights Day Commemoration — Tue Dec 15, 2:00 PM — Patriot Square at City Hall
item.description:
SAR and DAR Chapters Join Together to Honor America’s Founding Principles and New Bern’s Revolutionary Heritage During the Nation’s 250th Anniversary Year
NEW BERN, NORTH CAROLINA — On Tuesday, December 15, 2026, at 2:00 p.m., the New Bern Chapter, Sons of the American Revolution (SAR) and the Richard Dobbs Spaight Chapter of the National Society Daughters of the American Revolution (NSDAR) will present a special Bill of Rights Day commemoration and the dedication of a new granite and bronze marker honoring the historic New Bern Resolves.
The ceremony will take place at Patriot Square at City Hall, located at 300 Pollock Street in downtown New Bern.
The event brings together two important milestones in American history: the ratification of the United States Bill of Rights on December 15, 1791, and the adoption of the New Bern Resolves in August 1774, during the First Provincial Congress that was held in the then Thirteen Colonies.

item.title: Designing Web Surveys — Wed Feb 17, 2:00 PM
item.description:
This course will introduce methods for effectively designing web surveys to mitigate common mistakes that impact data quality and introduce measurement error. The course will focus on the following elements of web survey design – overall formatting and visual layout of screens, selecting and designing questions and response options (e.g., radio buttons, check boxes, grids, and open text fields), error and validation messaging, navigation elements, and usability. Special considerations for designing web surveys to accommodate mobile response will also be covered. This course will also offer practical guidance on selecting appropriate web survey platforms. However, this course will not provide instruction on the technical aspects of web survey programming or introduce programming languages. The course will draw from empirical literature on best practices coupled with practical considerations when designing and implementing web surveys.

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Thu Feb 18 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.title: NCMA Online Educator Course: Art and Math — Thu Feb 18
item.description:
This self-paced, ten hour course explores points of integration between the K-8 North Carolina Essential Standards in Math and Visual Art. The course includes opportunities for educators to learn strategies for using art to identify math concepts, apply math skills to create art, and to reflect within a collaborative peer learning community. Participants will gain an understanding of best practices in arts integration and will become more familiar with the North Carolina Museum of Art’s collection.
Each course module is divided into three sections: Define, Explore, and Practice. In Define, we introduce concepts, vocabulary, and works of art to stimulate thinking and help you begin identifying points of integration between art and math. In Explore, we ask you to deeply engage in those points of integration through participating in visual thinking routines and short activities that uncover math within art. item.title: Thanksgiving: Culinary & Cultural History — Sat Nov 21, 11:00 AM — Bennett Place State Historic Site
item.description:
Did you know that our modern Thanksgiving holiday largely has its origins in 1863? During the midst of the Civil War, President Lincoln proclaimed a day of Thanksgiving on the last Thursday of November to help heal the wounds of the nation and to restore peace and union.
Lincoln ultimately decided to make this Thanksgiving proclamation at the petition of Sarah Josepha Hale, editor of Godey's Lady's Book, who had advocated for such a holiday for over 15 years! This started an annual tradition which has been celebrated nationwide ever since.
For Lincoln and the loyal states in 1863, this Thanksgiving holiday allowed Americans to give thanks for major campaign victories (like Gettysburg) that year, for continued union of the loyal states, and blessings upon those who had lost loved ones in the war.

item.title: Fort Macon Daily Tour - 1:00 pm — Sat Nov 21, 1:00 PM — Fort Macon State Park
item.description:
A free guided tour of Fort Macon is available daily at 1:00 p.m. during the non-summer season from mid Oct. to mid April.
Tours last about 45 minutes.
Meet at the fort entrance. Pets are not allowed inside the fort.

item.title: Gobbles & Wobbles — Sat Nov 21, 1:00 PM — Carvers Creek State Park – Long Valley Farm Access
item.description:
November is the month when everyone seems to have turkey on the brain. Well, come out to the park and learn about the wild turkeys found here in our woods! There will be a fun craft that you can take home.
